findings.reason: the fork is the node's first trace step and its two arms point at different fixes (make a local hold queue vs. correct the routing so the review reaches local), so a node following the Why spends its diagnosis on states the cited path cannot produce instead of naming the mechanism that actually skipped the queue.
findings.text: the Why states both that "Flight resolves that review to clive, which is the project's `local_backend`" and that the queue was skipped "either [because] `is_local` was false, since it compares the resolved backend with `local_backend`, or the run carried a shadow lineage"; but `is_local = backend_name == local_backend and bool(local_backend)` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1460-1461`), so a review resolved to clive cannot also have `is_local` false, and `plan_review.dispatch_code_review` passes no `lineage_override` to `dispatch` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2771-2788`), so it can never carry a shadow lineage — leaving both named candidates excluded by the plan's own evidence and the real cause untraced
